key_insight: A dual topological-derivative framework uses one enriched 3-D stress analysis to both remove material and predict crack-driving energy release rates, enabling fracture-aware topology optimization.
engineering_relevance: This lets engineers design brittle structures that are not only lightweight but also less prone to crack initiation, with direct relevance to high-stakes 3-D components.
method: Level set topology is parameterized with radial basis functions and updated via optimization.
An interface-enriched finite element method computes stresses on the uncracked geometry.
Dual topological derivatives are used to nucleate holes and estimate boundary energy release rates; a p-mean aggregates the crack-risk measure.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 3-D numerical examples, including the L-bracket benchmark, to demonstrate the framework’s fracture-mitigation capability.
watch_item: The approach depends sensitively on stress accuracy and on assumptions such as penny-shaped crack nucleation and maximum hoop stress criterion, so robust implementation is critical.
paper_title: $\partial^2 ( \mathrm{TO} ) $: A Dual Topological Derivative-Based Enriched Topology Optimization for Fracture Mitigation in 3-D Brittle Solids
